title: Service Operations Platform
summary: Job requests, assignments, approvals, and records in one internal system.
details: A concept for a facilities services company with field teams. Office staff log requests, assign jobs, and track approvals, and managers see every job from request to sign-off in one place.
challenge: Requests arrive by phone, email, and chat. Assignments live in a spreadsheet, approvals in email threads, and no one has a full picture of which jobs are open, late, or waiting on sign-off.
solution: A single job record that moves through clear stages, with assignments, approval steps, and a full activity history. Staff work from a board of open jobs; managers filter by team, status, or due date.

title: Clinic Booking System
summary: Online appointments, staff schedules, and patient reminders in one place.
details: A concept for a small multi-practitioner clinic. Patients book an open slot online, staff manage daily schedules from one calendar, and the front desk sees every appointment at a glance.
challenge: Appointments are booked through calls and private messages and written in a logbook. Double bookings happen, reminders depend on someone remembering, and the front desk spends much of the day coordinating.
solution: Online booking tied to each practitioner's real availability, a shared calendar for the front desk, and a reminder workflow before each visit. Rescheduling updates the calendar immediately.

title: Inventory and Sales Tracker
summary: Stock levels, product records, and daily sales tracked in one system.
details: A concept for a growing retailer with a stockroom and two counters. Every product has one record, stock updates as sales and deliveries are logged, and low-stock items are flagged early.
challenge: Stock is counted by hand into two spreadsheets that rarely match. Items run out before anyone notices, and month-end reconciliation takes most of a weekend.
solution: One product catalog where every delivery, sale, and adjustment is recorded against the item. Stock levels are always current, and items below their reorder point appear on a daily list.

title: Customer Relationship Hub
summary: Customer profiles, purchase history, and follow-ups for a retail team.
details: A concept for a specialty retailer with repeat customers. Staff look up a customer at the counter, see past purchases and notes, and schedule follow-ups so no inquiry is forgotten.
challenge: Customer details are kept in notebooks and personal phones. When a staff member is away, follow-ups are missed and returning customers have to repeat themselves.
solution: One profile per customer with contact details, purchase history, and every interaction. Follow-up tasks are assigned to the team, with a pipeline view of open inquiries.

title: Operations Dashboard
summary: Key business figures and team activity on a single admin screen.
details: A concept for a delivery business with several dispatch teams. Managers check the day's key figures, filter by date range or team, and spot trends without exporting spreadsheets.
challenge: Daily figures are compiled by hand from several sources and shared as a report the next morning, so problems are noticed a day late.
solution: A dashboard that brings activity into one view: summary figures, trends over time, and a breakdown by team and status, with filters and role-based access.

title: Coworking Space Website
summary: A fast, mobile-first website with membership plans and tour bookings.
details: A concept for an independent coworking space. Visitors compare membership plans, see the space, and book a tour from a site built to load quickly on any phone.
challenge: The space is promoted only through social media posts. Prospective members cannot easily compare plans or book a visit, so inquiries arrive as scattered messages.
solution: A clear website with plan comparisons, a photo-led tour of the space, and a tour booking form. Content is easy for the team to update without a developer.
